items.summary: The geopolitical picture on Saturday May 30 morning is defined by the overnight aftermath of Trump's Situation Room meeting, convened on the WPA Day 90 hard deadline (Friday May 29) to make a 'final determination' on the Iran MOU — which CNN confirmed concluded without announcing a decision. As of Saturday morning, Trump has not publicly confirmed or rejected the 60-day MOU framework. Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesperson confirmed on May 29 that Iran and the US remain in contact but the MOU has not been finalized. Trump posted on social media demanding Iran agree to 'never have a Nuclear Weapon or Bomb' and that Hormuz be 'immediately open, no tolls, for unrestricted shipping traffic' — language consistent with reported deal terms but framed as ongoing demands, not a signed commitment. Deal architecture as defined at negotiator level: 60-day ceasefire extension; Hormuz reopening with Iran removing all mines within 30 days; proportional lifting of the US naval blockade as commercial shipping resumes; US sanctions waivers; Iran commitment not to pursue nuclear weapons; US commitment to discuss further sanctions relief during the 60-day window. White House confirmed negotiators have agreed to the MOU structure; Trump's approval is the outstanding principal-level step. The Khamenei approval gap is Day 1: Mojtaba Khamenei has remained out of public view communicating only via couriers since the 'broad principles' CBS/Axios signal (May 29). No formal Khamenei endorsement has been issued. The Shamkhani 'fantasy' nuclear-control statement (May 27) extends to Day 3 without Khamenei direct public correction. The symmetric dual-principal approval absence — Trump Situation Room without announcement, Khamenei courier-architecture without endorsement — constitutes the dominant deal-risk vector for Saturday. JPost framing: US-Iran ceasefire deal agreed upon, hangs on Trump and Khamenei approval. It appears unlikely Trump will sign before receiving definitive word that Khamenei has approved. Hormuz Day 92, Naval Blockade Day 49, Project Freedom Pause Day 25. WPA Day 91 — Day 1 past the hard 90-day constitutional deadline — without enforcement action, CENTCOM repositioning, or kinetic resumption overnight. The administration's 'hostilities terminated' posture (invoked May 1) remains operative; enforcement absent court ruling or congressional action leaves the posture intact near-term.

analyst_summary: May 30, 2026 Morning — Hormuz Day 92, Naval Blockade Day 49, Project Freedom Pause Day 25, WPA Day 91 — Day 1 Past Hard Constitutional Deadline, Warsh Day 16, Acting DNI Day 9. Vibe 3: holding. The May 30 Saturday morning session opens on the aftermath of Trump's Situation Room meeting — convened May 29 on the WPA Day 90 hard deadline date — which CNN confirmed concluded without announcing a decision. Both principal-level approvals remain outstanding: Trump's 'final determination' is pending post-Situation Room; Khamenei's formal MOU endorsement is absent Day 1 from the 'broad principles' CBS/Axios signal. Iran FM confirmed on May 29 that contact is ongoing but the MOU has not been finalized. The White House confirmed negotiators have agreed to the MOU structure; Trump's approval is the outstanding step. It appears unlikely Trump will sign before receiving definitive word that Khamenei has approved. Deal architecture defined at negotiator level — 60-day ceasefire extension, Hormuz reopening with mine removal within 30 days, proportional blockade lift, sanctions waivers, Iran commits not to pursue nuclear weapons — but the JPost/Euronews framing captures the structural stall precisely: both principals must still say yes. WPA Day 91 arrived without enforcement action, CENTCOM repositioning, or kinetic resumption; the administration's 'hostilities terminated' posture holds as operative framing. Markets closed Friday at records: S&P 500 7,580.06 (+0.22%), Nasdaq 26,972.62 (+0.2%), Dow 51,032.46 (+0.72%); May: S&P +5%, Nasdaq +8%+; S&P 500 posted ninth consecutive weekly gain, longest streak of 2026; Brent slipped on deal optimism. Warsh Day 16 silent; June FOMC 16 days; Cleveland nowcast 4.18%; April CPI 3.8% (beat consensus); PCE highest in nearly three years; personal saving rate 2.6% (June 2022 low) — structural economic deterioration accumulating without Chair communication. PNW: Saturday is transitional (70s-80s) as the heat dome builds toward the confirmed Heat Advisory for Sunday May 31 — 8 AM to 11 PM PDT, up to 92°F, potential record for Portland International Airport (record: 89°F, 1992). NIFC June 1 east Cascades above-normal onset T-2. Oregon fire Day 23; BLM Day 17; Level 1 Central OR Day 13; Bureau of Reclamation Day 10. Reconciliation 2.0: June 1 Trump deadline all but certain to be missed — Thune confirms senators will 'pick up where we left off' June 1; return date, not floor vote. Portland City Council reconvenes June 1 with $172M shortfall T-32. Israel-Lebanon ceasefire Day 14 holding; June 2-3 talks T-3. CISA clean streak Day 27; Shamkhani IRGC cyber risk Day 3. Measles ~1,992; school window 8 days active. Vibe 3 holds. Saturday is a deliberation day — Trump 'final determination' and Khamenei formal endorsement remain the symmetric dominant forward signals. Sunday is the test: 92°F Heat Advisory + NIFC T-2 + dual-principal deal stall = highest-coherence compound stress day of the 2026 cycle.
